paper_title: Recent Progress in Hole-Transporting Layers of Conventional Organic Solar Cells with p-i-n Structure

qa_pairs.question: Why does the use of PEDOT:PSS as a hole-transporting layer often lead to the degradation of organic solar cell devices?
qa_pairs.answer: PEDOT:PSS is acidic in nature, typically having a pH between 1 and 2. This high acidity corrodes the Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) anode, which causes indium to diffuse into the photoactive layer, ultimately leading to device degradation.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in Hole-Transporting Layers of Conventional Organic Solar Cells with p-i-n Structure

qa_pairs.question: What are the champion performance metrics reported for organic solar cells utilizing a tungsten oxide (WOx) modified PEDOT:PSS hole-transporting layer?
qa_pairs.answer: Organic solar cells using a WOx-modified PEDOT:PSS hole-transporting layer achieved a champion fill factor (FF) of 80.79% and a certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.15%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in Hole-Transporting Layers of Conventional Organic Solar Cells with p-i-n Structure

qa_pairs.question: How does the origin of the built-in potential (Vbi) in organic solar cells differ from that in silicon-based photovoltaics?
qa_pairs.answer: In silicon solar cells, the built-in potential (Vbi) is created through the doping of a homojunction. In contrast, the Vbi in organic solar cells primarily originates from the work function (WF) difference between the two electrodes.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in Hole-Transporting Layers of Conventional Organic Solar Cells with p-i-n Structure

qa_pairs.question: Compare the electrical conductivity and HOMO energy level of the self-doping polymer PCP-Na to standard PEDOT:PSS.
qa_pairs.answer: PCP-Na exhibits a deep HOMO level of -5.22 eV and an electrical conductivity of 1.66 × 10⁻³ S cm⁻¹. This conductivity is superior to the 1.35 × 10⁻³ S cm⁻¹ measured for standard PEDOT:PSS. Additionally, PCP-Na is pH-neutral, unlike the acidic PEDOT:PSS.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in Hole-Transporting Layers of Conventional Organic Solar Cells with p-i-n Structure

qa_pairs.question: Why is electrochemical polymerization considered a more effective method for fabricating conjugated microporous polymer (CMP) films compared to surface-initiated or cross-linking methods?
qa_pairs.answer: Electrochemical polymerization allows for the in situ fabrication of CMP films, which bypasses the issues caused by the poor solubility of CMPs synthesized through standard surface-initiated or cross-linking methods. This improved processability makes it more suitable for photovoltaic device applications.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in Hole-Transporting Layers of Conventional Organic Solar Cells with p-i-n Structure

qa_pairs.question: How does the hole mobility of a device using the conjugated polyelectrolyte CPE-K compare to one using PEDOT:PSS?
qa_pairs.answer: The hole mobility of a CPE-K based device is 1.5 × 10⁻⁵ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, which is approximately two orders of magnitude higher than the mobility of a PEDOT:PSS-based device, which is 1.2 × 10⁻⁷ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in Hole-Transporting Layers of Conventional Organic Solar Cells with p-i-n Structure

qa_pairs.question: Explain the role of metal nanoparticle size in enhancing the light absorption of organic solar cells when incorporated into the hole-transporting layer.
qa_pairs.answer: The size of metal nanoparticles, such as silver (Ag), is critical for light harvesting; particles larger than 50 nm significantly enhance light absorption due to strong plasmonic scattering effects. In contrast, smaller nanoparticles (below 30 nm) provide minimal enhancement to light absorption.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in Hole-Transporting Layers of Conventional Organic Solar Cells with p-i-n Structure

qa_pairs.question: What is the primary advantage of using PCPDT-T as a hole-transporting layer regarding film thickness?
qa_pairs.answer: PCPDT-T exhibits high thickness insensitivity. This property allows organic solar cells to maintain a stable power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 7.1% even when the thickness of the HTL is increased to 50 nm.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in Hole-Transporting Layers of Conventional Organic Solar Cells with p-i-n Structure
